title: A2A Vendor Core Execution Contract
description: Normalized request/response envelope for Vendor Core adapters (Arista, Cisco, Juniper, ...). This schema formalizes the response envelope already used in practice (see response_schema.py in a2a-containment-core, MIT), written as a shared convention so that the common multi-vendor UI (a2a-console) can read every vendor the same way.

trace_id.description: Unique identifier correlating this contract instance across the init/observe/act/report lifecycle.

query.description: Natural-language instruction as entered by the operator. Routing to read/write/diagnose is classification-driven (NL intent classification), not an explicit client-supplied operation code.

route.description: The normalized operation category this query was classified into, independent of vendor-specific mechanism (NETCONF, eAPI, PyEZ, etc.).

vendor_key.description: Vendor/NOS identifier (e.g. arista_ceos, juniper_ptx, cisco_nxos). Selects the Vendor Core adapter and its NOS_PROFILES entry in the shared UI.

routed_to.description: URL of the downstream agent this request was dispatched to (e.g. the vendor's NETCONF write agent).

status.description: Normalized outcome status, shared across all Vendor Core Hubs regardless of vendor. `dry_run` and `no_change` are treated as OK outcomes; `failure`/`error`/`blocked` are not.

summary.description: Short, human-readable one-line summary of the result, shown directly in the operator UI.

result.description: Vendor/route-specific inner payload (e.g. generated NETCONF XML, eAPI commands, diff output). Intentionally left open-shaped per vendor and route; the outer envelope is what is normalized, not the inner detail.

human_confirmation_required.description: Reserved for a future diagnose -> approval -> execute flow. True signals the UI should show an approval prompt before proceeding.

recommended_action.description: Reserved for a future diagnose -> approval -> execute flow. A suggested corrective command, when applicable.
